newsitem.title: ITALY: Albania's Fino and Italy's Prodi to discuss crisis.
newsitem.headline: Albania's Fino and Italy's Prodi to discuss crisis.

text.p: The prime ministers of Italy and Albania will discuss the crisis in the Balkan country on Monday in Rome after European Union foreign ministers meet in Brussels to work out an aid mission.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office said on Sunday that he and Albania's Bashkim Fino would discuss Albania's appeal for help to restore order and stability.
A statement said they would also talk about the effect on Italy of an exodus of nearly 11,000 Albanian refugees since March 13.

It reiterated Italy's position that Albanians who would be in danger if they returned home or who needed medical care could stay temporarily but others, particularly those considered a threat to public safety, would have to return.
Italy has already repatriated several hundred undesirables, including prisoners who escaped from Albanian jails in the chaos and refugees who broke the law after their arrival.
Italy says the rest will be repatriated after the situation in Albania returns to normal.
The EU foreign ministers in Brussels will work out a blueprint for security measures to assist the humanitarian relief mission.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini told reporters on Sunday that European humanitarian aid to Albania was urgently needed but embarking on a military operation was "not opportune".
Dini added, however that the aid would need a protection force "because there is a risk that it will end up in the hands of armed bands".

Fino's talks with Prodi will come on the eve of a meeting between the Albanian prime minister and EU foreign ministers travelling to Rome to Tuesday to mark the 40th anniversary of the founding of the European Economic Community.
Two Italian military helicopters from the southern port of Brindisi flew in nearly two tonnes of medical supplies to the rebel stronghold of Vlore in the south on Sunday morning.
Italy also plans to fly medical aid to the government-controlled capital Tirana in the north of the country, at Fino's request.
Dini said it might become necessary for Italy to help control the Albanian ports from which the refugees are leaving. This would need Albanian permission, he said.
Rome and Tirana are negotiating an agreement to allow the Italian navy to patrol within the Balkan country's territorial waters in an effort to stem the exodus and assist the humanitarian operation.
On Sunday more Albanian refugees arrived in southern Italy after a lull of three days caused by bad weather.
A military boat carrying some 130 people arrived early on Sunday and at least one other boat was expected during the day.
The coastguard took a pregnant Albanian woman off one of the boats and took her to a hospital in Brindisi.
